quests.instruction: Two of these fruits have seeds scattered through the flesh. Which one is different?
quests.hint: Look inside: where are the seeds?
quests.explanation: Watermelon and kiwi have seeds scattered through their flesh, while mango has one large stone in the center.
quests.funFact: Mango is a stone fruit, like peach and plum.

quests.instruction: Two of these fruits have shells that peel away from the flesh. Which one is different?
quests.hint: Think about how you get to the flesh.
quests.explanation: Lychee and longan have shells that are peeled away, while the skin of a plum is eaten.
quests.funFact: Both lychee and longan have a shiny dark seed inside.

quests.instruction: All three of these fruits look fuzzy. Which one grows differently from the other two?
quests.hint: Think about where each one grows.
quests.explanation: Peach and apricot are stone fruits that grow on trees, while kiwi has tiny seeds and grows on a vine.
quests.funFact: Peach, apricot and kiwi all have fuzzy or velvety skin.

quests.instruction: Two of these are citrus fruits. Which one is not?
quests.hint: Think about juicy segments and sour juice.
quests.explanation: Lemon and lime are citrus fruits, while pear belongs to a different family and has a core.
quests.funFact: Pears are related to apples.

quests.instruction: Which pair of fruits are close cousins?
quests.hint: Think about names and looks.
quests.explanation: Peaches and nectarines are close relatives. Pineapples are not apples, and bananas and lemons are unrelated.
quests.funFact: Both peaches and nectarines are stone fruits with a hard pit.

quests.instruction: Which pair of fruits both have segments you can pull apart?
quests.hint: Think about citrus.
quests.explanation: Mandarins and grapefruit are citrus fruits with juicy segments. Peaches and apricots have pits, and apples and cherries do not have segments.
quests.funFact: The segments make citrus fruit easy to share.

quests.instruction: You want to test whether a paper bag helps bananas ripen faster. What is a fair test?
quests.correctAnswer: Put one banana in a bag and a similar one outside, then compare
options: Put a banana in a bag and an apple outside, then compare
Put one banana in a bag and a similar one outside, then compare
Put both bananas in the same bag and just wait
quests.hint: Only one thing should be different.
quests.explanation: A fair test changes only one thing, the bag, and keeps everything else the same.
quests.funFact: Scientists call this a controlled experiment.

quests.instruction: In the banana test, which things should stay the same?
quests.correctAnswer: Same kind and ripeness of banana, same room temperature
options: Nothing, because every banana is exactly the same
Same kind and ripeness of banana, same room temperature
The color of the bag and the day of the week
quests.hint: Think about what could change the result.
quests.explanation: Keeping the bananas and the room the same makes sure the bag is the only difference.
quests.funFact: Keeping conditions the same makes results trustworthy.

quests.instruction: Which question can be answered with an experiment?
quests.correctAnswer: Do cut apples with lemon juice brown more slowly?
options: Which fruit looks the prettiest on a plate?
Which fruit is the best fruit in the world?
Do cut apples with lemon juice brown more slowly?
quests.hint: A test needs something you can measure or observe.
quests.explanation: You can test browning by watching the apples, but opinions like prettiest or best cannot be measured.
quests.funFact: Good scientists start with a question they can test.

quests.instruction: What happens right after bees pollinate an apple blossom?
options: The tree drops all its leaves
quests.hint: Think about what blossoms are for.
quests.explanation: After pollination, the blossom's base swells and the fruit begins to form.
quests.funFact: Many fruits take weeks or months to grow after pollination.

quests.instruction: A fruit tree starts as a seed. What stage comes next?
quests.hint: Think about what a sprouted seed is called.
quests.explanation: A seed sprouts into a small plant called a seedling before it grows into a tree.
quests.funFact: Roots usually appear first when a seed sprouts.

quests.instruction: A seed lands in good soil with water and warmth. What can happen?
quests.correctAnswer: It can sprout into a seedling
options: It turns into juice inside the soil
It can sprout into a seedling
It becomes a flower right away
quests.hint: Think about what seeds need.
quests.explanation: With soil, water and warmth, a seed can sprout into a seedling.
quests.funFact: Some seeds can wait for years before conditions are right to sprout.

quests.instruction: Ana picked 12 apples, Ben picked 9 and Cy picked 15. Who picked the most?
quests.hint: Compare the three numbers.
quests.explanation: 15 is more than 12 and 9, so Cy picked the most apples.
quests.funFact: Counting and comparing helps farmers plan their harvest.

quests.instruction: Ana picked 12 apples, Ben picked 9 and Cy picked 15. How many apples did they pick altogether?
quests.hint: Add 12, 9 and 15.
quests.explanation: 12 plus 9 is 21, and 21 plus 15 is 36 apples.
quests.funFact: Adding in small steps makes bigger sums easier.

quests.instruction: A chart shows how many students like each fruit: banana 8, orange 6, mango 10. Which fruit is the class favorite?
quests.hint: Look for the biggest number.
quests.explanation: Mango has the highest number of votes, 10, so it is the class favorite.
quests.funFact: Charts help us compare numbers at a glance.

quests.instruction: It is red and has one hard pit. Which fruit fits both clues?
quests.hint: One of these has seeds on the outside and one has a core.
quests.explanation: Cherries are red with one hard pit. Strawberries have tiny seeds on the outside, and apples have a core.
quests.funFact: Cherry season is short, so fresh cherries are a seasonal treat.

quests.instruction: It is orange inside, grows on a vine and has a hollow center with seeds. Which fruit?
quests.hint: Check where each fruit grows.
quests.explanation: Cantaloupe grows on a vine. Mango grows on a tree, and papaya grows on a tall, tree-like plant.
quests.funFact: Cantaloupe is called rockmelon in some countries.

quests.instruction: It is small, grows in bunches on a vine and has tiny seeds or none. Which fruit?
quests.hint: Check the growing form first.
quests.explanation: Grapes grow in bunches on vines. Blackberries grow on thorny bushes, and plums grow on trees and have a pit.
quests.funFact: Some grape varieties are grown for eating, and others for raisins or juice.

quests.instruction: A friend says tomatoes are not fruits because they are not sweet. What is a good reply?
quests.correctAnswer: Fruits are defined by how they grow, not by how sweet they are
options: You are right, because only sweet foods can be fruits
Tomatoes only count as fruits when they are cooked in sauce
Fruits are defined by how they grow, not by how sweet they are
quests.hint: Remember what fruits grow from.
quests.explanation: A fruit grows from a flower and holds seeds, whether it tastes sweet or not.
quests.funFact: Cucumbers, peppers and pumpkins are fruits for the same reason.

quests.instruction: A friend says bananas grow on trees. Is that exactly right?
quests.correctAnswer: Not quite, they grow on tall plants with soft trunks
options: Yes, banana plants are true trees with wooden trunks
Not quite, they grow on tall plants with soft trunks
No, they grow on low bushes near the ground
quests.hint: Remember what the trunk is made of.
quests.explanation: Banana plants look like trees, but their trunk is made of wrapped leaf bases instead of wood.
quests.funFact: Banana plants can grow taller than a house.

quests.instruction: A friend says all fruits grow on trees. Which fruit shows this is not true?
quests.hint: Think about a low plant.
quests.explanation: Strawberries grow on low plants, while apples and mangoes grow on trees.
quests.funFact: Melons and grapes grow on vines too.

quests.instruction: A friend says that if you swallow a watermelon seed, a plant will grow in your tummy. Is that true?
quests.correctAnswer: No, seeds need soil, water and light to sprout
options: No, seeds need soil, water and light to sprout
Yes, the seed will sprout in your stomach juices
Yes, but only if you swallow many seeds at once
quests.hint: Think about what a seed needs to grow.
quests.explanation: Seeds need soil, water, warmth and light to sprout, so a swallowed seed just passes through the body.
quests.funFact: Watermelon seeds pass through the body without sprouting.

quests.instruction: A saying claims one fruit can keep all illness away. What is a sensible view?
quests.correctAnswer: Fruit is part of a healthy diet, but no food is a guarantee
options: One special fruit can protect you from every illness
Fruit is part of a healthy diet, but no food is a guarantee
Fruit is unhealthy because it contains natural sugar
quests.hint: Think about balance.
quests.explanation: Fruit helps with a healthy diet, but no single food can guarantee good health.
quests.funFact: Eating many different foods, getting sleep and being active all help.

quests.instruction: Is a red apple always sweeter than a green apple?
quests.correctAnswer: No, taste depends on the kind and ripeness
options: No, taste depends on the kind and ripeness
Yes, red apples are always the sweetest ones
Yes, green apples are never sweet at all
quests.hint: Color is only one clue.
quests.explanation: Taste depends on the kind of apple and how ripe it is, not just on its color.
quests.funFact: Some green apples are sweet, and some red apples are tart.

quests.instruction: If you plant a mango seed in cold, snowy land, what is likely to happen?
quests.correctAnswer: It would struggle in the cold
options: It would grow fruit in a week
It would turn into an apple tree
It would struggle in the cold
quests.hint: Think about where mango trees grow best.
quests.explanation: Mango trees need warm weather all year and struggle in the cold.
quests.funFact: Mango trees are often grown in pots indoors in cooler places.

quests.instruction: If a lime stays on the tree until it is fully ripe, what color does it turn?
quests.hint: Think about its cousin, the lemon.
quests.explanation: Limes are usually picked green, but fully ripe ones can turn yellow.
quests.funFact: Lemons also change from green to yellow as they ripen.

quests.instruction: A coconut falls into the sea and drifts to a warm beach. What may happen?
quests.correctAnswer: It may sprout into a new palm
options: It may sprout into a new palm
It sinks and turns to sand
quests.hint: Think about floating seeds.
quests.explanation: Coconuts float, so ocean currents can carry them to new beaches, where they may sprout.
quests.funFact: Coconut palms have spread to many tropical islands this way.

quests.instruction: Which of these facts about fruits is true?
quests.correctAnswer: Fruits grow from flowers and hold seeds
options: Fruits grow from flowers and hold seeds
All fruits are sweet and soft to eat
Fruits only grow high up on trees
quests.hint: Think of everything you have learned about how fruits form.
quests.explanation: Fruits grow from flowers and hold seeds. They can be sweet, sour or savory, and they grow on trees, vines, bushes and low plants.
quests.funFact: Even tomatoes, peppers and cucumbers are fruits.

quests.instruction: Why are there so many different kinds of fruit?
quests.correctAnswer: Plants grow in many places and spread seeds in many ways
options: All fruits are copies of one ancient fruit that changed color
Fruit shops decide which shapes and sizes to grow
Plants grow in many places and spread seeds in many ways
quests.hint: Think about trees, vines, bushes and seeds.
quests.explanation: Fruits differ because plants grow in different places and use different ways to protect and spread their seeds.
quests.funFact: Over thousands of years, people have also bred many new kinds of fruit.

quests.instruction: Which shows good fruit-handling habits?
quests.correctAnswer: Wash hands, rinse fruit and leave sharp cutting to a grown-up
options: Skip washing to save time and keep the flavor
Cut the fruit yourself with the sharpest knife you can find
Wash hands, rinse fruit and leave sharp cutting to a grown-up
quests.hint: Think about hygiene and safety.
quests.explanation: Washing hands, rinsing fruit and leaving sharp knives to grown-ups keeps fruit safe and fun.
quests.funFact: These habits are the same ones used in professional kitchens.
